prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent pixel mascot for a website report's closing message.
Input image 1 is the edit target: the already approved Dabom dark purple cat.
Change its pose to sitting comfortably upright on its haunches, facing mostly forward, with two small front paws together on the ground. Keep the same recognizable charcoal-purple fur, lavender inner ears, cream pixel eyes, tiny friendly face, cream envelope with a lavender heart, chunky stair-step pixel silhouette and subtle soft texture inside the pixels. The envelope can rest against its chest. Preserve the character, not the standing/walking pose.
Composition for later CSS tail animation: single complete cat, seated body centered slightly left; a long curved tail extends from the lower right hip out toward the right and curls upward. The tail must be clearly separated from the head and upper body by transparent negative space, touching the body only at the low hip root. Leave generous transparent margins around the whole cat and tail. Body from roughly 25% to 62% of image width, tail on the right from about 60% to 85%. Tail tip below the ears.
Output a single still neutral pose, NOT animation frames or a sprite sheet. True transparent background, square canvas. No text, no floor, no scenery, no shadows behind the cat, no extra characters. Keep this cute simple retro pixel style, not smooth vector, not realistic, not 3D.
implementation: SittingMessengerCat clips the original transparent PNG into overlapping body and tail layers. Only the tail rotates. The existing prefers-reduced-motion rule disables animation.
